note.question: How should an on-demand platform delay, pool, or individually serve time-sensitive customers and charge them when sharing saves cost but customer values arrive privately over time?
note.overview: This is a dynamic mechanism-design paper: customers privately report values and the platform optimizes an incentive-compatible, individually rational allocation and payment rule over stochastic arrivals.

models.name: On-demand service sharing and dynamic pricing
models.summary: This is a dynamic mechanism-design paper: customers privately report values and the platform optimizes an incentive-compatible, individually rational allocation and payment rule over stochastic arrivals.
objects: Privately informed time-sensitive customers (two agents in the benchmark and an unlimited arrival stream in the generalization)
inputs: Customer 2's arrival time is stochastic and observed
The platform commits ex ante to a historyand report-contingent direct mechanism
Each customer's valuation theta_i is private; types are i.i.d. from a publicly known distribution
decisions: Platform chooses service timing, shared versus individual allocation, and type-contingent payments
In the general model the platform decides whether to provide service
Customers report private valuations or select the equivalent option from an implemented dynamic menu
assumptions: Customers and platform are risk neutral; customer service value decays at rate delta and monetary payoffs are discounted at rate r>0
Customer values are i.i.d. draws from a publicly known continuous distribution satisfying monotone hazard rate, with each realization privately known
Customer 2's arrival time is exponential with rate lambda
In the base model two suppliers are available at time zero, a shared service creates no extra customer disutility, and shared or individual service costs the platform c
The platform commits to a direct mechanism; expected transfers are used in the derivation, with an equivalent payment rule satisfying ex post individual rationality
